In mathematics, the '''quantum dilogarithm''' is a [[special function]] defined by the formula

:<math>
\phi(x)\equiv(x;q)_\infty=\prod_{n=0}^\infty (1-xq^n),\quad |q|<1
</math>

It is the same as the [[q-exponential|''q''-exponential]] function <math>e_q(x)</math>.

Let <math>u,v</math> be "''q''-commuting variables", that is elements of a suitable noncommutative algebra satisfying Weyl's relation <math>uv=qvu</math>. Then, the quantum dilogarithm satisfies Schützenberger's identity
:<math>\phi(u) \phi(v)=\phi(u + v),</math>
Faddeev-Volkov's identity
:<math>\phi(v) \phi(u)=\phi(u +v -vu),</math>
and Faddeev-Kashaev's identity
:<math>\phi(v)\phi(u)=\phi(u)\phi(-vu)\phi(v).</math>

The latter is known to be a quantum generalization of [[Dilogarithm#Identities|Rogers' five term dilogarithm identity]].

'''Faddeev's quantum dilogarithm''' <math>\Phi_b(w)</math> is defined by the following formula:

: <math>\Phi_b(z)=\exp
\left(
\frac{1}{4}\int_C
\frac{e^{-2i zw }}
{\sinh (wb) \sinh (w/b) }
\frac{dw}{w}
\right),</math>

where the contour of integration <math>C </math> goes along the real axis outside a small neighborhood of the origin and deviates into the [[upper half-plane]] near the origin. The same function can be described by the integral formula of Woronowicz:

: <math>
\Phi_b(x)=\exp\left(\frac{i}{2\pi}\int_{\mathbb R}\frac{\log(1+e^{tb^2+2\pi b x})}{1+e^{t}}\,dt\right).
</math>

[[Ludvig Faddeev]] discovered the quantum pentagon identity:

: <math>\Phi_b(\hat p)\Phi_b(\hat q)
=
\Phi_b(\hat q)
\Phi_b(\hat p+ \hat q)
\Phi_b(\hat p),
</math>
where <math>\hat p</math> and <math>\hat q</math> are [[self-adjoint]] (normalized) quantum mechanical momentum and position operators satisfying Heisenberg's commutation relation

:<math>[\hat p,\hat q]=\frac1{2\pi i}</math>

and the inversion relation

: <math> \Phi_b(x)\Phi_b(-x)=\Phi_b(0)^2 e^{\pi ix^2},\quad \Phi_b(0)=e^{\frac{\pi i}{24}\left(b^2+b^{-2}\right)}. </math>

The quantum dilogarithm finds applications in [[mathematical physics]], [[quantum topology]], [[cluster algebra]] theory.

The precise relationship between the ''q''-exponential and <math>\Phi_b</math> is expressed by the equality

:<math>\Phi_b(z)=\frac{E_{e^{2\pi ib^2}}(-e^{\pi ib^2+2\pi zb})}{E_{e^{-2\pi i/b^2}}(-e^{-\pi i/b^2+2\pi z/b})},</math>

valid for <math>\operatorname{Im} b^2>0</math>.
